answer: Persistent work-credit ledger. Each agent identity accrues reputation only through verified task completions; credit is non-transferable and decays if idle. A clone starts at zero credit, so it cannot bid on high-value contracts until it independently completes the same low-tier work—costing the attacker real compute and time per clone. The ledger runs on a shared terrace of task queues where new identities are throttled to copper-tier jobs, and only seasoned accounts reach the island of premium contracts. Cloning N identities costs N times the entry workload, while honesty pays once.
